cards.title: World Notes: How a Lighthouse Works
cards.sub: A real person and place behind this week's game
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: A lighthouse is a tall tower with a bright light at the top. At night, the light warns ships away from rocks.
Each lighthouse flashes in its own pattern, so sailors can tell which one they are looking at.
Grace Darling's family moved into the new Longstone Lighthouse in 1826, when she was 10. It still stands on its rocky island today.

notes.wordParts: Prefixes and suffixes from this year: re- = again, un- = not, trans- = across, inter- = between, -ful = full of, -less = without.
notes.grammar: Year review: capitals for names and the first word, a comma after an opening part, apostrophes for belonging and joined words, and irregular past forms like went and took.
notes.spelling: Long words: find the vowels, split between them, read each chunk, then push the chunks together. Rescue = res + cue.
notes.wgrd: Text 2 shows courage instead of telling it. Mira’s heart hammers and her feet want to turn around, but she walks onto the bridge.
vocab: having or showing courage; willing to act even when afraid
continuing to try even when things are hard
a quality that shows good character
doing the right thing even when no one is watching

mods.label: Opti shows you how
mods.script: Let's try all three parts with a different sentence from Text 2. Mira's heart hammered. Part one, read like a reader. Mira is very scared. Part two, read like a writer. The author never says scared. She shows it with the body: a heart that hammers like a hammer on wood. Part three, write your own. My turn: Sam's hands shook on the rope. Now it's your turn with the author's sentence. Write one sentence in each box.

mods.script: Three questions, in full sentences. One, two details that show Mira's courage. Two, how Mira fits what Text 1 says. Three, which way of showing courage you think is stronger, and why.

virtue.name: courage
virtue.title: Courage Watch: Is someone being brave?

items.t: For weeks, Mira finds a reason to walk the other way when the big boys take things.
items.why: Walking away is not courage yet. Mira changes later in the story.

items.t: Mira walks onto the bridge, even though her feet want to turn around.
items.why: She is scared, and she acts anyway.

items.t: When the small boy asks, Mira says she was very afraid.
items.why: It takes courage to admit you were scared.
